source.title: On Affine Homotopy between Language Encoders
source.authors: R. Chan; Reda Boumasmoud; Anej Svete; Yuxin Ren; Qi-Peng Guo; Zhijing Jin; Shauli Ravfogel; Mrinmaya Sachan; Bernhard Scholkopf; Mennatallah El-Assady; Ryan Cotterell

record.tranche_reason: The paper empirically measures affine alignment between language encoders and relates it to downstream-task similarity, using finite representation sets and several alignment measures rather than testing scale-driven convergence with the original claim's method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports empirical affine-alignment errors, correlations with downstream similarity, layer and task patterns, and rank-related results. Theoretical bounds and results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. Table 1's individual cells are not assigned because the flattened text does not reliably align its row labels and values; its stated aggregate comparison is recorded.
record.test_reason: The study fits affine maps between 25 MultiBERT seeds, ELECTRA and RoBERTa on GLUE training-set embeddings and reports max-error mapping distances (Fig. 1/4). These bear on V3 (seed convergence) and V4 (linear interchangeability). It finds mappability is asymmetric and tied to the target encoder's rank, and states the encoders are generally not exactly affinely related. Its main empirical result, that intrinsic similarity correlates with downstream similarity, validates the measure rather than testing convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that affine alignment is asymmetric yet informative of, and upper-bounds, downstream similarity. Affine intrinsic similarity is consistently predictive of downstream behaviour and reveals an order among encoders, partly explained by rank differences. They also say affine homotopy is appropriately sensitive to seed changes, and that encoders may not be exactly affinely related in practice.
record.recipe_differences: Uses finite-set affine alignment and correlations with downstream similarity across language encoders; it does not reproduce the original studies' method. The paper focuses on affine homotopy and its task-related implications.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with task/dataset, layer, direction of mapping, encoder rank, and similarity measure. The text says the early-layer pattern is task-independent but later-layer patterns diverge.

fits_no_version.finding: Affine intrinsic distance between encoders correlates with extrinsic downstream-prediction distance, with ρ ranging 0.08–0.52 across GLUE tasks. Linear CKA tracks extrinsic similarity less well than alignment-based measures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity under alignment-based measures predicts similarity of downstream linear-probe behaviour better than kernel (CKA) measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Artificially rank-truncated MultiBERT encoders give roughly symmetric affine distances. Same-rank pairs map more easily at lower rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Encoder rank mismatch drives asymmetry of affine mappability.

record.problems: The empirical alignment tests use finite training-set representations and approximate max-error optimization; the authors note that some distances are approximated by optimizing mean squared error, and that rank estimates depend on numerical precision. The Hausdorff–Hoare comparisons use costly approximations. Several plotted results have no numeric values in the text, and Table 1's flattened individual values could not be reliably assigned.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's individual correlation cells were omitted because the flattened text does not reliably align all values with row labels; its explicit aggregate comparison is retained in r7. Figure-only alignment-error values beyond the qualitative layer and rank patterns were not individually extracted.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no models of different families compared by size.
No feature- or unit-level matching, and no shared-subspace analysis. Only affine max-error mappability among MultiBERT seeds.
No stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment. No held-out or downstream loss of the mapped representation is reported as a mapping-quality figure.
No interpretable features, neurons or circuits.
Does not report how convergence levels change across metrics, neighbour counts or out-of-distribution inputs; only how well each metric predicts downstream similarity.
No test of plateau or of shared data or objectives as causes.

missing.what: Per-layer and per-task max-error alignment magnitudes among seeds and across models (layers 1, 4, 8, 12; six tasks). Needed to judge how close seed and cross-model affine alignment is.
missing.locator: Figure 1 and Figure 4 heatmaps (color scale ~0–10 max L2 error)

missing.what: Authors' statement that MultiBERT representations are generally not exactly affinely related.
Individual Table 1 ρ/PCC values per method and dataset. Some alignment-method Spearman values are near zero or negative.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is mainly theoretical; its experiments validate an asymmetric similarity measure rather than test convergence. The main text says results are on SST-2 and MRPC, but the appendix and figures cover six GLUE tasks, with MNLI and QQP truncated to 10K samples. Fig. 1 distances are computed by MSE optimisation with max error evaluated, an approximation of the paper's own distance. No baseline or chance level for mapping error is given, so 'little loss' under V4 cannot be judged.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of alignment increasing as models grow.
No vision-language model comparison or paired image-caption representations.
Measures affine mappability among differently initialized MultiBERTs, not whether individual features recur or whether the same shared subspaces are learned under other feature-specific measures.
Tests affine maps on finite datasets; does not test stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are analyzed.
Compares several similarity methods and datasets/layers, but does not vary neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports incomplete/exact affine mappability and asymmetry, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment, nor whether alignment plateaus with scale.

rows.operation_detail: Compared alignment-based intrinsic measures and linear CKA against extrinsic similarity

conditions.value: Orthogonal Procrustes, CCA, PWCCA, linear CKA, and affine alignment

rows.measure: Authors' aggregate characterization of correlations with downstream similarity
rows.value: The paper reports significant, large linear correlations for alignment-based methods overall, and says linear CKA captures extrinsic behavior less faithfully.
rows.uncertainty: The text says Table 1 marks p-value < 0.01 with an asterisk; individual table values are not assigned here.
rows.note: The conclusion is the authors' stated aggregate comparison; individual Table 1 cells were omitted because the flattened labels and values are ambiguous.
rows.check: This compares how well similarity measures predict downstream similarity (CKA predicts worse). It is not a finding that convergence itself depends on the metric. Table 1 cells are mixed: several alignment-method Spearman values are near zero or negative (e.g. -0.147*), so 'large correlation in all' fits PCC better than ρ.

rows.value: The text reports that some encoders are consistently easier to map to, largely independently of which encoder is mapped from; this trend is task-independent in early layers.
rows.note: The paper reports the pattern but gives no numeric values in the text for this layer grouping.
rows.check: Mappability between seeds and models is direction-dependent: some encoders are consistently easy to map to, others are not. No baseline or loss threshold is given, so 'little loss' can't be confirmed. V6/V7 links removed.

rows.subject: MultiBERTs (aggregate across model pairs)
rows.operation_detail: Truncated representation matrices by SVD to create rank-deficient encoders, then measured affine mapping error

conditions.value: artificially reduced ranks from 20% to 90% of full rank

rows.value: The text reports that lower-rank encoders of the same rank become easier to map between, and that the distances are rather symmetric; the plotted trend is not numerically stated.
rows.note: Artificial rank reduction is a tested condition, not a null control.
rows.check: Rank deficiency is induced artificially by SVD truncation. This is a controlled check of the theory, not natural representation convergence.

relationships.condition: 25 MultiBERT seeds, affine max-error alignment across layers 1–12 on GLUE tasks
relationships.reason: Seed-to-seed mappability is asymmetric: some seeds are easy targets, others are not. The pattern is task-independent only in early layers (r8, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Across 25 seeds and layers 1–12, some seeds were easier alignment targets than others; this pattern was task-independent only in early layers.

source_check.reason: Section 7 reports direction-dependent mappability among seeds, with task-independent patterns in early layers that diverge in later layers. This qualifies correspondence by direction, layer and task.

relationships.condition: Affine maps among ELECTRA, RoBERTa and MultiBERTs; mapping direction and target rank
relationships.reason: Mappability depends on direction. Target-encoder rank correlates with mapping-to distance (ρ 0.31–0.61), not mapping-from. Authors state encoders are generally not exactly affinely related (r8–r12).
relationships.display_finding: Target rank correlated with mapping-to distance at ρ=0.31–0.61 but not mapping-from distance, and encoders were generally not exactly affinely related.

source_check.condition: Affine maps among ELECTRA, RoBERTa and MultiBERTs; mapping direction and target rank
source_check.reason: Affine mappability depends on direction and target encoder. Target rank correlates with mapping-to distance on RTE, MRPC and QQP (ρ = 0.312, 0.609 and 0.389), with no significant mapping-from correlations. Appendix B also cautions that representations may not be exactly affinely related.

source_check.notes: The row findings are qualitative; they do not establish an absolute little-loss threshold. Appendix B explains that maps minimize MSE and are evaluated by maximum error, approximating the theoretical distance.
